ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Preventive Visit — Thomas Jefferson — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Mr. Jefferson is a 47-year-old cabinet secretary with episodic migraine without aura on propranolol prevention and an old right wrist injury, who comes for his yearly preventive visit four weeks after his six-week review. He has had one migraine attack in the past four weeks, treated with sumatriptan and naproxen and gone within two hours. He has taken propranolol 120 mg each evening for four weeks without dizziness, breathlessness or low mood, and he notices cold fingers on cool mornings. His diary shows acute medicine on one day this month. He has had no tetanus booster for more than ten years and has never had a colon cancer screening test. [S]

Follow-up: Three-month review in four weeks. FIT kit returned by mail. HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B results by phone. Second hepatitis B vaccine dose in one month. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1790-08-13: three-month review: response to prevention, disability, acute medicine use and the plan ahead. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 18 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent, a close friend, and a health care proxy form was completed; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. He said that what matters most to him is being able to think, read and write, and to keep his independence. He chose not to record specific treatment preferences today. The plan will be revisited yearly or after any serious illness. [S]
